summary.title: [Article endings] Hidden share rail remains in the keyboard tab order
summary.one_line_description: The floating share rail is transparent before the scroll threshold, but all five invisible links can still receive keyboard focus.

bug_1.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/components/SocialShareRail.astro - share-rail anchors, Lines 15-20 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/scripts/social-share.ts - function: `updateVisibility`, Lines 1-9 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/styles/global.css - selectors: `#sh-box` and `#sh-box[data-visible='true']`, Lines 1235-1251 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/js/scr.js - legacy scroll visibility contract, Line 1

issue_description.description: The migrated rail hides itself with `opacity: 0` and `pointer-events: none`, but it does not use `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, `inert`, or managed tab indices. A direct Chromium keyboard check on `/blog/breakup-energy` at `scrollY = 0` found `data-visible="false"`, computed opacity `0`, and tab index `0` on all five anchors. Repeated Tab presses focused Share on Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, email, and Copy page link while the rail remained invisible. The legacy scroll script removed the rail from layout while hidden. This affects every article and long-form route that enables `floatingShare` and gives keyboard users invisible focus stops before the control is available visually.
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Keyboard behaviour** | Rail links enter the tab order only when the rail is visible | Five transparent rail links receive focus before the user scrolls | | **Visual focus** | Every focused control is visible | Focus moves through controls with computed opacity `0` | | **Legacy parity** | Hidden rail is unavailable until the scroll threshold | Migrated rail is visually hidden but still interactive by keyboard | | **Recommendation** | Synchronise visual visibility, accessibility exposure, and tab order, then add a keyboard regression test before and after the threshold | Current CSS changes only opacity and pointer input |

summary.title: [Article endings] Share links no longer preserve route-specific legacy payloads
summary.one_line_description: The fixed rail and supplement ending generate different share messages and query parameters from the audited route contracts.

bug_2.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/components/SocialShareRail.astro - share URL construction, Lines 7-12 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/components/ShareLinks.astro - bottom Twitter URL construction, Lines 8-13 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/pages/supplements/index.astro - `ArticleEnding` invocation, Lines 20-31 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/js/scl.js - function: `updateSocialShareLinks`, Lines 33-52 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/supplements/index.html - legacy supplement Twitter share anchor, Lines 5332-5339

issue_description.description: `SocialShareRail.astro` replaces the recorded rail payloads with one hard-coded Twitter phrase, omits the Facebook title, changes the LinkedIn endpoint and title payload, and changes the email subject and body. The legacy script derived Twitter text from page metadata, included the document title for Facebook and LinkedIn, and used `Worth a read` plus `You might find this interesting: <URL>` for email. The supplement bottom share link also falls through to the generic `Interesting read` text because the route does not provide `twitterText`, although the legacy route used the supplement-specific `Check out this supplement guide` message. The legacy supplement URL contains a `.co` typo, which should be corrected as a verified technical fix without discarding the approved route-specific message. These differences are observable when a visitor activates the restored article-ending controls.
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Twitter rail** | Page metadata title, canonical URL, and `via=musclehacking` | Generic `Interesting read` payload on every route | | **Facebook and LinkedIn** | Canonical URL plus the recorded page-title payload | Facebook drops title; LinkedIn changes endpoint and drops title | | **Email rail** | Subject `Worth a read` and explanatory body with the URL | Subject becomes the page title and body is only the URL | | **Supplement bottom share** | Supplement-specific share copy with the corrected canonical host | Generic article share copy | | **Recommendation** | Model the audited share payload per control and route, preserving approved copy while correcting only the known host typo | Current shared defaults erase route-specific behaviour |

summary.title: [Content extraction] Article migration recreates duplicated endings
summary.one_line_description: Rerunning the checked-in blog migration writes legacy post navigation and disclosure markup into content that already receives a shared `ArticleEnding`.

bug_3.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/scripts/migrate-legacy-content.mjs - legacy body cleanup and output, Lines 53-85 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/layouts/ArticleLayout.astro - shared `ArticleEnding` render, Lines 51-64 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/healthy-low-calorie-foods.md - current manually separated article content - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/blog/healthy-low-calorie-foods.html - legacy disclaimer and navigation source, Lines 542-561

issue_description.description: The extraction selector removes forms, Share, Comment, prompts, and scripts, but it does not remove `#post-nav` or the disclosure nodes between `#comm` and `#post-nav`. An in-memory execution of the selector against the audited sources left one `#post-nav` on every blog article and left the Amazon disclosure on `healthy-low-calorie-foods`. The current Markdown files have been cleaned separately, so the built output is correct today. However, rerunning the repository migration utility overwrites all twelve Markdown files with retained legacy navigation, after which `ArticleLayout.astro` appends another shared navigation. The affected disclosure route also receives both retained disclosure markup and `AffiliateDisclaimer`. The checked-in migration is therefore not repeatable and can recreate the exact duplicate or misplaced ending defect the shared layout was introduced to prevent.

summary.title: [Verification] Passing parity gates do not enforce the complete ending contract
summary.one_line_description: The E2E and distribution checks pass while route order, mobile coverage, share payloads, and hidden keyboard focus remain unverified.

bug_4.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/ui-parity.spec.ts - test: `UI-12 restores previous and next article navigation at desktop and mobile`, Lines 553-610 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/ui-parity.spec.ts - test: `reopened article endings restore share, comment, disclaimers, wrapping, and floating rail`, Lines 612-686 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/a11y/site.spec.ts - representative axe-only route loop, Lines 1-20 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/scripts/verify-dist.mjs - article-ending checks, Lines 80-107

issue_description.description: The ending matrix test skips the mobile Playwright project entirely, then validates all twelve articles only at a forced desktop viewport. Its child-order assertion uses `expect.arrayContaining`, which accepts any order and extra elements even though the reopened requirement calls for an exact route-specific sequence. The mobile portion of UI-12 covers only `breakup-energy` and the one-sided calculator-guide article; the four section routes are checked only for two link counts on desktop. No check asserts the floating-rail destinations or removes hidden rail links from the keyboard sequence. The accessibility suite scans only six representative routes with axe and does not perform keyboard traversal. The distribution verifier checks only `newsletter < share < navigation` for blog routes, so it does not verify Comment, disclosure placement, floating rail presence, route-specific share payloads, section endings, or the complete route-state-viewport matrix. Both `pnpm verify:dist` and the two focused article-ending E2E tests passed during this audit while bugs 1 and 2 remained reproducible.
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Route matrix** | Exact ending sequence and controls on every applicable article and section route | Complete article loop is desktop-only; section assertions are presence-only | | **Responsive coverage** | Every previous-only, next-only, and two-sided ending checked at required mobile widths | Mobile checks cover two article examples, not the route matrix | | **Ordering** | Exact ordered child sequence with route-specific disclosure rules | `arrayContaining` accepts reordered and additional nodes | | **Keyboard and destinations** | Visible focus and exact external payloads are asserted | Hidden focusable rail links and changed share URLs pass | | **Recommendation** | Drive one authoritative ending fixture across every route, viewport, order, payload, focus state, and no-JavaScript response | Current independent checks leave the reopened integration contract incomplete |
